Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 18-Nov-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  Computer Vision-III [CSE_4031]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                      Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                A drone captures aerial images of a construction site to monitor progress and detect structural        (5)  
  cracks.  
  A)           Illustrate how digital image processing steps help to extract structural details and detect possible  
  defects.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  B)           Examine how Power-Law Transformations are used to control image contrast in photographs                (5)  
  captured under varying illumination conditions.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2)                Illustrate how edge detection techniques help in obtaining important structural details from digital   (5)  
  images.  
  A)           Compare the working principles of the Laplacian and Canny edge detection methods  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  B)           Apply the concept of the Histogram of Oriented Gradients descriptor to identify and represent the      (5)  
  shape and structure of objects within an image. Discuss with a suitable real time application  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3)                A drone captures rooftop images for inspection, but the photos appear misaligned and distorted due (5)  
  to the camera's tilt. Apply geometric transformations to adjust the tilted drone images and discuss in  
  A)           detail.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           In an AR game, players use their phone camera to find virtual coins, but lighting changes and    (5)  
  camera shake cause feature mismatches, making the coins appear misplaced. Apply the RANSAC  
  algorithm to detect and remove incorrect feature points, helping the game build a stable surface  
  model and accurately place virtual coins on real surfaces.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)                Apply the learned motion estimation framework to detect abnormal motion patterns in video streams (5)  
  and discuss in detail.  
  A)  
  Page #1

Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)                In a video tracking application, a system needs to estimate how an object moves between                (5)  
  consecutive frames. Utilize the Lucas-Kanade method to estimate the motion of objects across  
  consecutive frames.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5)                        Develop an intruder detection system using face recognition for a secure facility where individuals    (5)  
  may wear masks, glasses, or hats and explain the recognition pipeline to create a reliable method  
  A)                that ensures accurate identification of unauthorized persons under varying appearance conditions.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)                Apply a computer vision-based activity detection model to develop an elderly care monitoring         (5)  
  system that observes indoor movements and detects signs of falls or distress. How would you apply  
  these techniques to automatically identify normal vs. abnormal activities and trigger alerts in real  
  time?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
